lean.fidelity_note: The paper begins with the maximal smooth solution supplied by general existence theory, whose lifespan could still be infinite at this stage. The formal statement instead constructs a smooth odd Euler solution on $[0,T_\infty)$, proves the stated initial-data and earlier-interval convergence in every $C^{m,1/2}$ norm, and compares that solution conditionally with every maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same data. It does not assert general maximal-solution existence. The preterminal Euler existence and convergence conclusions are present; Corollary 8.3 later proves that this constructed solution itself is maximal at the finite time $T_\infty$.

statements.markdown: **Proposition 8.1.** The data $U_j(0)$ converge in every $C^{m,1/2}$ to an odd divergence-free field $u_0$. In particular, $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^3)$. Let $u$ be the maximal smooth solution of the Euler equations from $u_0$, with maximal time $T_*>0$, supplied by Section 1. Then $T_*\ge T_\infty$ and, for every $T<T_\infty$ and integer $m\ge0$, $U_j\to u$ in $C([0,T];C^{m,1/2})$. The solution is smooth and odd on $[0,T_\infty)\times\mathbb T^3$.
